clue.text: That old gramophone record by Benn is getting stuck in a groove

parts.note: a mono record, made before stereo, is shortened to mono
Tony Benn, the British Labour politician

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a vintage disc of a politician's speeches as tediously repetitive.
explanation.walkthrough: TONY Benn was a long-serving British Labour politician. 'getting stuck in a groove' plays on the gramophone picture but defines the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting stuck in a groove is a picture of dull sameness, the tedium of a routine that never changes.

clue.text: Adult friend goes round an old city

indicators.note: one piece going round another encloses it

parts.note: a mate is a friend
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A grown-up pal travels around a historic city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Sumerian city, is a crossword favourite; 'an' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a fully grown person, one who has reached full development.

clue.text: Diana's wayward nymphs

indicators.note: letters gone wayward have strayed out of their proper order

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana's unruly attendant spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges DIANAS; the possessive gives its S here as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Water nymphs of Greek myth lived in rivers, springs and fountains.

clue.text: Story about Tourist Trophy is just idle gossip

indicators.note: one word about another goes round it

parts.note: a tale is a story
TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Talk of the Isle of Man motorbike races is dismissed as mere chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT races are a famous motorcycle event in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is trivial chatter about others, mere idle talk.

clue.text: Case of one Scotsman turning savage

indicators.note: turning sends the words before it back the other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Mon is a stock Scots form of address for a man
native is an old, now offensive, word for an uncivilised person

explanation.surface: An instance of a Scot going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the pair 'one Scotsman' together, giving NOMI; 'Case' is the grammatical subject case, not a box.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the subject of a verb takes the nominative, one of the noun cases.

clue.text: An edge from one of Australia's leading batsmen

explanation.surface: A narrow advantage gained courtesy of a top Australian cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Allan Border captained Australia at cricket and was one of its highest run-scorers.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge or margin of something is its rim, and Allan Border was a leading Australian Test batsman.

clue.text: Gaffes to make behind the scenes

indicators.note: letters used to make something are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Blunders committed out of the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges the eight letters of GAFFES TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Away from the stage and the audience's sight is backstage, out in the wings.

clue.text: After a month with the salesman it is worn out

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: After thirty days on the road with a travelling seller, it is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: DEC, then REP, a sales representative, then IT as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means enfeebled by age or use, dilapidated and past its best.

clue.text: Tried again by thrusting match into the thatching material

indicators.note: thrusting one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: reed is used to thatch roofs
a test is a cricket Test match

explanation.surface: A match retried after being pushed into thatching straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrusting' is the container signal, with 'into' as its link; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Subjected to a second trial, checked a further time.

clue.text: Those spare hours one has when money is scarce

definitions.text: Those spare hours one has when money is scarce

parts.words: Those spare hours one has when money is scarce
parts.note: spare is read as lean or meagre rather than free, describing a hard-up period

explanation.walkthrough: 'spare hours' suggests leisure, but spare here means lean: a lean stretch of life when cash runs short.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean, impoverished period of life is a phrase for hard times when cash is short.

clue.text: Fabric remnant sent down to the third man?

definitions.text: sent down to the third man?

explanation.surface: A scrap of cloth is posted off to a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball cut off the bat behind square on the off side runs down to the fielder at third man.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap trimmed from cloth, and a cricket cut stroke played on the off side that travels toward the third man fielder.

clue.text: Odorous house payments swallow up unemployment benefit

indicators.note: one word swallowing another means the second sits inside the first

parts.note: rent is what a tenant pays for a house
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Smelly housing costs eat up a jobless person's welfare money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odorous' sits at the front as the definition; 'the dole' is the everyday British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redolent gives off a strong smell, so it is fragrant or smelly.

clue.text: Wrests awkwardly away and throws all over the place

indicators.note: letters wrenched awkwardly out of place come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone yanks things off and flings them everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly away' rearranges the six letters of 'Wrests'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter things is to throw them all over the place, as one scatters straw.

clue.text: Wordless poetry?

parts.note: poetry with nothing written in it would be empty, plain verse with no words

explanation.walkthrough: The term really means unrhymed iambic pentameter; the question mark lets 'blank' be read as empty, so verse with no words in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrhymed verse in iambic pentameter, as Shakespeare and Milton used, jokingly read as empty lines.

clue.text: German prison camp child raised in a cave with dripping

definitions.text: raised in a cave with dripping

parts.note: a Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A child brought up in a cave by a POW camp, soaked by drips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like 'brought up' of the child, but belongs to the definition: the formation rises from the cave floor.
explanation.definitionFit: This deposit grows upward from a cave floor where mineral-laden water drips onto it.

clue.text: What builders use for hanging on

explanation.surface: Builders' kit, for clinging to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging on' suggests gripping tight, but means executing someone on a gallows platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders erect a framework of poles and planks, and a gallows platform was used for executions.

clue.text: A sea-going soldier relaxes on the side of an easy chair

definitions.text: the side of an easy chair
definitions.note: singular in the clue, while the answer names the two arms of the chair

parts.note: RM is a Royal Marine
rests means relaxes

explanation.surface: A marine unwinds on the edge of a comfy chair.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for Royal Marines, soldiers who serve at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised supports for elbows at each side of an armchair.

clue.text: Group of families executed by the Trident shipyard

explanation.surface: A gang of relatives put to death by a submarine yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' suggests killing but means carried out: a yard building Trident submarines fills a sub order.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a rank between order and family, and a submarine contract carried out by a shipyard.

clue.text: A number cut vermin in order to get around the problem

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: put in order means the letters are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A count of rats cut down so as to dodge an infestation problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges CUT VERMIN into IRCUMVENT, after C, the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass or evade a difficulty is to find a way round it.

clue.text: The RAC is his club of course

definitions.text: The RAC is his club of course

parts.words: The RAC is his club of course
parts.note: the Royal Automobile Club is a motorist's body, and on a golf course a club of this name hits from the tee

explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist belongs to a motoring club, and the longest-hitting golf club shares the name.

clue.text: Popular man takes in real dope

parts.note: a hero is a man people admire

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes in genuine information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests inside information, but is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard opiate is drug slang's genuine article.

clue.text: Wanders aimlessly in the deep snow

explanation.surface: Someone roams without purpose through heavy snowfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks of snow heaped by the wind share the word for wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: To move without purpose is to roam, and wind-piled banks of snow are snowdrifts.

clue.text: Litter from the back seats of the theatre?

definitions.text: the back seats of the theatre?

explanation.surface: Rubbish left behind in the rearmost seats at a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish, but means a brood of piglets; the far row is the one at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sow's litter of piglets, and a distant row of seats read as two words.

clue.text: Listen to another invitation to join a group by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to go by how the call is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: calling 'over here!' invites someone to come and join you

explanation.surface: Someone hears a second invitation to come and join some people.
explanation.walkthrough: The call 'over here' is said just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone else's words unintended is to eavesdrop on another person.

clue.text: The batsman's leg is in the correct playing position for football

definitions.text: in the correct playing position for football

explanation.surface: A footballer's position is judged legal from where a player's leg stands.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket leg side is also the on side, and in football a player not offside is in a legal position.

clue.text: Play golf if the whist tournament has been cancelled

definitions.text: if the whist tournament has been cancelled

explanation.surface: Go out for a round on the links if the card evening is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: A whist drive is a British social card tournament; cancelled, it is a drive off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the first shot from the tee starts a golf round, and a whist drive that is called off is off.

clue.text: What the 8th Army fought for was leave

explanation.surface: A remark on the wartime cause of a British army, and on furlough.
explanation.walkthrough: The British 8th Army fought the North African campaign of the Second World War in the Western Desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The 8th Army battled over North African sand wastes, and to abandon someone is to leave them.

clue.text: This type of ball is taken by navigators

explanation.surface: A kind of ball that sailors pick up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ball bearings are steel balls in machinery; navigators take bearings to fix a course.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings are small steel spheres in machines, and compass directions are what navigators take.
